description:
Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG, commonly known as Porsche,[a] is a German automobile manufacturer specializing in luxury, high-performance sports cars, SUVs and sedans, headquartered in Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. The company is owned by Volkswagen AG, a controlling stake of which is owned by Porsche Automobil Holding SE, usually shortened to Porsche SE. Porsche's current lineup includes the 911, Panamera, Macan, Cayenne and Taycan[8].
The origins of the company date to the 1930s when German Bohemian automotive engineer Ferdinand Porsche founded Porsche[9] with Adolf Rosenberger,[10][2] a key figure in the creation of German automotive manufacturer and Audi precursor Auto Union,[11] and Austrian businessman Anton Piëch, who was, at the time, also Ferdinand Porsche's son in law. In its early days, it was contracted by the German government to create a vehicle for the masses, which later became the Volkswagen Beetle.[12] Aft

title: Porsche 901
description:
Porsche 901 was the name originally intended for the Porsche 911.
By the early 1960s, Porsche project design numbers had reached into the 800s. For instance, Porsche's 1962 F1 model was called Porsche 804.
At the Internationale Automobil-Ausstellung (Frankfurt Motor Show) in Frankfurt in September 1963, Porsche presented its successor to the Porsche 356 as the 901. It took several more months until the cars were manufactured for sale to customers. Between 14 September and 16 November 1964, 82 cars were built[1] and the 901 was presented in October at the 1964 Paris Auto Salon. Porsche Cayman S

Cayman S 3.4-litre under acceleration

The Cayman S' performances equalled the performance of Porsche's flagship models at the time. Rally driver Walter Röhrl lapped the Nürburgring Nordschleife track in a Cayman S equipped with optional 19" wheels, PCCB, and PASM[29] in a time of 8 minutes, 11 seconds.[30][31] The time for a standard Cayman S, as published by the manufacturer, was 8 minutes, 20 seconds.[32] In contrast, Röhrl recorded 8 minutes, 15 seconds in a 911 Carrera.[33][34]
A Cayman prepared and run by private team of Jürgen and Uwe Alzen finished fourth overall (of 220 entrants) in the 2007 Nürburgring 24 Hour race, ahead of two flagship Porsche 997 GT3 RSR's, a 997 GT3 Cup, and a 996 GT3 Cup.[35] Another two privateer Caymans, entered by CSR and MSpeed, finished 22nd and 117th overall, respectively. The Sport Turismo has the same silhouette as the Cross Turismo wagon and storage space. But it has the lower ride height of the Taycan sedan, giving it a racier, performance-minded look — and feel.",[57] and as such is treated as a new body type.
